newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators say met Rubin on IRS farm policy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators say met Rubin on IRS farm policy.

text.p: Two Democratic senators said they met with Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Tuesday to express their opposition to an Internal Revenue Service policy on deferred contract farm commodity sales.

Senators Byron Dorgan, D-ND, and Max Baucus, D-MT, said they pressed their case that the IRS is making an error in its interpretation of how deferred payment farm commodity contract sales are treated when calculating the Alternative Minium Tax.
The senators in a statement said the talk with Rubin was "encouraging" and that the Treasury secretary promised a response by Friday.
The senators said they asked Rubin to withhold any IRS enforcement action on the policy until Congress has an opportunity to enact legislation that would reverse the IRS policy.
"The policy would have the practical effect of forcing many farmers to pay taxes on payments they have not yet received," the statement said.
